# #11002: Wired Xbox 360 controller broken on macOS Sequoia

- **Labels:** —

## Report

MacOS Sequoia added native support for wired Xbox 360 controllers using the Game Controller framework. This seems to have broken some assumptions that we had about Xbox 360 controller support on macOS in the HIDAPI driver. We assume that [we will always be talking through the 360Controller driver](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/1787d6ca5c249c7ebabf885e63c96b1a5f3f61cc/src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c#L83C8-L97
) if we see a Xbox 360 wired controller on macOS. 360Controller speaks a slightly different protocol than the real Xbox 360 hardware, so these assumptions cause problems when we're receiving real unmodified reports from actual hardware.

The biggest problem is that the Y axis of both analog sticks is inverted. The reason is code here, presumably for a 360Controller quirk: https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/1787d6ca5c249c7ebabf885e63c96b1a5f3f61cc/src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c#L270-L274

The second issue is that rumble doesn't work through the HIDAPI device. One reason is the [special 360Controller rumble packet](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/1787d6ca5c249c7ebabf885e63c96b1a5f3f61cc/src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c#L200-L223), but even getting rid of that hack doesn't result in working rumble. It's not clear if this is a limitation of macOS or something we're doing wrong.

Finally, the controller itself shows up twice in SDL. HIDAPI picks it up as an IOHID device and the MFI backend picks it up as a GCController. The latter seems to be what we really want to be using, since it has both a proper mapping and working rumble support.

This is all fairly easy to reproduce with `testcontroller`. By default you get both MFI and HIDAPI devices, but you can set `SDL_JOYSTICK_MFI=0` and `SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI=0` to switch between the 2 duplicate devices.

It seems like we have basically two main options:
- Figure out how to tell 360Controller apart from real hardware in the HIDAPI driver and figure out how to get rumble working through HIDAPI (if it's even possible at all)
  - This seems like it will be a mess, since it will probably require adding a whole bunch of OS-specific stuff into the otherwise generic `SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c` file.
  - Sending raw output reports might not even be possible due macOS's driver having control of the device
- Figure out a way to prefer GCController over HIDAPI for these Xbox 360 controllers
  - We could prioritize GCController over HIDAPI for _all_ controllers, but I'm not sure if some controllers have more functionality through HIDAPI than GCController
  - We could prioritize GCController over HIDAPI for just certain controllers, but I don't know if there's an exhaustive list of all Xbox 360 devices that macOS Sequoia supports now. It could also change in a future OS update.
